purpose: Category-level research for the physical AI stack beyond GPUs: networking, optics, memory/HBM packaging, power/grid, funded interconnection, reliability, cooling, water and industrial automation. Research-only; no site/UI/scoring changes.
categoryRead: The physical-AI thesis remains strong, but it now splits sharply between verified/funded demand and headline interconnection requests. Reuters reports more than 700 GW of US data-centre electricity requests - over 10x estimated current US data-centre power use - while Texas halted new grid connections and launched an audit and other utilities tightened deposit/funding requirements. Some demand forecasts fell after deposits were imposed. This does not invalidate real hyperscaler demand: August ISM still shows Production 58.3, Prices 71.1 and shortages/rising prices across electrical/electronic components, memory, semiconductors, copper and wire. The investment conclusion is to prefer customer-funded backlog, deposits, named projects and cash conversion over speculative MW pipelines.

newRiskLens.name: Funded load quality / ghost demand
newRiskLens.evidence: US data-centre grid requests exceed 700 GW; Texas and several utilities are screening ownership, funding, deposits and duplicate requests.
newRiskLens.implication: Supplier order books backed by real customers become more valuable than utility load forecasts or developer announcements. Utilities/developers that overstate future load face capex, ratepayer and valuation risk.
newRiskLens.confirmation: Verified/deposit-backed MW remains strong while speculative requests are cancelled and supplier booked orders hold.
newRiskLens.invalidation: Audits show most requests are fully funded and committed, leaving headline queue totals broadly intact.
newRiskLens.nextTest: Texas/PJM/AEP/Exelon audit/deposit data and named hyperscaler interconnection milestones.

BDC.read: Record Q2 orders remain stronger evidence than demand forecasts. Keep focus on book-to-bill and named data-centre/industrial wins.

GNRC.read: Roughly $1.6bn data-centre backlog remains useful because it is booked demand; audit the customer/project quality and backlog conversion rather than broad data-centre MW estimates.

AMKR.read: NVIDIA demand and customer prepayments support utilisation/financing quality; heavy capex and FCF conversion remain constraints.

0522.HK.role: HBM TCB/hybrid bonding + photonics + AI-server SMT
0522.HK.read: HBM/advanced-packaging equipment demand remains supported by component scarcity; qualification/order conversion and valuation are the next tests.

SLB.read: Kelvion remains a differentiated thermal-management entry; require integration, customer quality and 2028 target execution before further promotion.

AGKO.read: High-priority IPO watch because time-to-power can bypass grid queues, but ghost-demand evidence makes customer contracts and final IPO leverage/valuation even more important.

existingCoreCrossRead.GEV: Generation/grid demand remains high quality when orders are named/contracted; do not use aggregate interconnection queues as demand evidence by themselves.
existingCoreCrossRead.ETN: Switchgear/power-management shortages remain confirmed by ISM; Sep 1 price weakness improved entry asymmetry but high real yields remain a multiple headwind.
existingCoreCrossRead.PWR: Transmission/substations remain essential for verified large-load interconnections; require project awards and backlog, not utility queue totals.
existingCoreCrossRead.POWL: Order/backlog evidence remains strong; valuation/execution constrain entry quality.
existingCoreCrossRead.VRT: Cooling/power-management demand remains real, but valuation discipline and verified customer deployment matter.
existingCoreCrossRead.FLEX: Planned Cloud & Power Infrastructure spin is strategically aligned, but the new load-quality screen should be applied to backlog/customer concentration before treating growth guidance as fully de-risked.
existingCoreCrossRead.YTLPOWR: Strategic power/data-centre exposure remains strong, but leverage/cash conversion and actual contracted utilization matter more than Malaysian data-centre announcement volume.
existingCoreCrossRead.ROK: Profitable factory/warehouse automation remains the preferred first-wave robotics/physical-AI expression.

augustISMPhysicalStack.signal: Physical activity is still expanding, but orders/backlog slowed while input inflation and delivery stress stayed severe. Electrical/electronic components, memory, semiconductors, copper and wire remain direct bottleneck evidence.

roboticsRead: No adoption-wave change: warehouse/fixed industrial automation first, cobots/mobile manipulation second, industrial humanoids third, open-world/general-purpose robots last. Current ISM production supports factory automation, but slower New Orders argues against a broad industrial-capex chase.

PWR/ETN/GEV/FLEX named orders and backlog conversion
